tool_args.rationale: All five observations are positive and lie at H = 0.16–0.48, far short of the target H = 21.5. In this window, different slow amplitudes and timescales can produce nearly identical responses but disagree on the long-horizon sign. The slow-horizon probe directly tests the predicted reversal before committing to a model.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the recalled dual-exponential adaptation law now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The recalled law omits the observed sink-gradient signature. Adding a sink term still leaves the slow amplitude and timescale poorly constrained by five short-window rows.
It costs less, but finer temporal sampling does not directly test whether the response reverses near the forecast horizon.
Neither recalled form accounts for the sink-gradient signature, and the Haldane law has no horizon dependence.
